descriptionChirho: The cardinal direction of east, the region where the sun rises, used as a geographical or cosmological orientation marker. Multilingual evidence uniformly maps to cardinal-direction terminology: Spanish 'oriente/orientes,' Hindi 'पूर्व' (pūrv = east, the standard directional term), Arabic 'الْمَشْرِقِ/المَشارِقِ' (al-mashriq / al-mashāriq = east / easts, from ش-ر-ق to rise/shine), Korean '동쪽/동쪽에서' (dongjjok = east), Swahili 'mashariki' (east, borrowed from Arabic). Used of the Magi coming 'from the east' (Matt 2:1-2), lightning flashing from east to west (Matt 24:27), the angel ascending from the east (Rev 7:2), and the kings from the east (Rev 16:12; 21:13).

The act or phenomenon of rising — specifically the rising of a celestial body (sun, star) or metaphorically the dawning of messianic light. Distinct from the directional sense because it denotes the event or process of rising rather than a fixed geographical reference. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'salida/aurora' (salida = rising, going out / aurora = dawn — not 'oriente'), Hindi 'उदय' (uday = rising, dawn — not 'pūrv'), Arabic 'مَشرِقِ/مُشْرِقٌ' (mushriq = shining/radiant, participial form emphasizing the action), Korean '떠오름/돋는 해가' (tteoorum = rising / dotneun hae-ga = the rising sun), Swahili 'mashariki ya' (rising of). Found in Matt 2:2 (the star 'at its rising'), Luke 1:78 (the 'dayspring/dawn from on high'), and 2 Pet 1:19 (the morning star rising in hearts).
